Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Anchor + stretch renewal — usage & capacity review

Camila —

Thanks again for the Q3 health check last week. We pulled our consumption data for the last 90 days and saw two things that are worrying: a sustained 35% increase in chat-generation tokens and several short latency blips during peak batch hours (attached). We are approaching the end of our current term and need to firm up renewal parameters.

High level asks:
- Can Redwood propose an anchor (renewal baseline) that covers our steady-state run rate and a separate stretch/burst corridor for spikes?
- We need ROI numbers to justify a larger commit to finance — total cost per 1M tokens at proposed anchor vs current run-rate.
- Any SLA/credits for the latency blips — those impacted user shipments last month and we need remediation language for the contract amendment.

Attached: 20261110-paloma-token-usage-q3.csv (hourly tokens, model mix, error traces).

Proposed meeting window: Thu 11/12 10–11am PT or Mon 11/16 1–2pm PT. Could you send a short pre-read?

Thanks —
Alyssa Chen
Head of Platform
Paloma Systems
alyssa@palomasystems.com

Alyssa —

Appreciate the dataset — that helps a lot. Ben and I dug into the CSV this morning and sketched a few directional numbers. Short answer: we can structure an anchor + stretch that (a) reduces unit price for committed baseline traffic, and (b) provides a bounded burst corridor with pre-provisioned capacity + burst credits so you don’t see latency blips while avoiding an oversized commit.

Pre-read attached: anchor-stretch-proposal-draft.pdf (ballpark pricing, burst corridor mechanics, suggested SLA credits for latency incidents). Key callouts:
- Baseline anchor: 12M tokens/month (your 90-day median ~9.2M, 75th pct ~11.8M).
- Stretch corridor: up to +40% on top of anchor with burst credit pool; unconsumed burst credits roll forward for one quarter.
- Unit economics: committed tier reduces per-1k-token cost by ~18% vs current on-demand; with the stretch uplift we model a blended cost reduction of ~10% vs today at projected Q1 volume.

Couple of asks before the call:
1) Can Tom provide a short list of the top 5 API routes (model + endpoint) driving the spikes? That will help us size dedicated pools vs shared routing.
2) Are you comfortable with a 60-day pilot for quantized variants on non-critical routes to validate latency/quality tradeoffs?

We can take Mon 11/16 1–2pm PT — I’ll send a calendar invite. Ben, can you bring the pricing sheet and a quick jitter/latency baseline? Karthik, please prepare a one-slide fallout/recovery credit template for contract language.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.com

Quick follow-up with the pricing sketch we discussed — pushing a short table into the thread so you can forward to finance. Numbers are conservative for now.

Pricing snapshot (draft):
- Current blended: $95 per 1M tokens (on-demand + some committed)
- Proposed anchor tier (12M/mo): $78 per 1M tokens (committed)
- Stretch consumption above anchor (up to 40%): $92 per 1M tokens, with first 20% of stretch drawn from burst-credit pool at $0 marginal
- Dedicated GPU pool option (if Paloma wants predictable p99 latency): additional $8k/mo for a small pool or a $0.02 per 1k token uplift for hybrid route (we model the pool if you want hard p99s)

I dropped the draft price table to our HubSpot deal for visibility: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/company/PL-2026-0043 (see Products > Proposed Pricing).

Camila / Ben —

Appreciate the clear options. Mon 11/16 1–2pm PT is confirmed for us. A couple of items to surface to legal and finance ahead of the call so we can come prepared:
- We need an explicit latency credit schedule tied to p99 > threshold during contiguous 30-minute windows; finance will want to know max credit exposure under the proposed anchor + stretch.
- We also need a concrete ROI table (annualized) that compares: current spend, proposed anchor-only renewal, and anchor+stretch with the predicted 10% blended reduction. Please include model-mix assumptions (which model families move to quantized variants).
- One more ask: if we commit to the anchor and take the quantized pilot, can we get a 30-day rollback window should quality regress for critical routes? That will help product teams sign off.

Tom will attach the top route list before the meeting (Tom: can you drop that by EOD Friday?).

Thanks — looking forward to the call.

Best,
Alyssa

Alyssa —

Thanks for the prep notes and for confirming the meeting. I’m attaching a one-page ROI recap (roi-modelmix-onepager.pdf) that lays out the annualized numbers across the three scenarios you asked for plus the model-mix assumptions. Summary bullets below and I’ll walk through during the call:

Summary (pre-read):
- Anchor-only (12M/mo): Net annualized cost change: 
  - Current baseline annualized: $1,140,000 (forecasted on-demand + commitments)
  - Anchor-only estimate: $1,075,200 (≈5.7% reduction; lower unit but less burst protection)
- Anchor + Stretch (12M anchor + 40% corridor): Net annualized: $1,026,000 (≈10% reduction vs current blended) with estimated risk-adjusted exposure 
  - Max credit exposure under proposed SLA bands: ≈$18k/yr (assuming 3 threshold incidents)
- Pilot plan: 60-day quantized pilot on two non-critical endpoints — expected to cut inference cost for those routes by ~22% with negligible quality delta in our evaluation set; we include a 30-day rollback clause for the two routes in the amendment.

Next steps I’ll take after the call:
1) Produce a formal amendment draft with the SLA credit table and rollback language (DocuSign link will be included).
2) If you approve, legal and finance sign-off route typically takes 7–12 business days for customers of your size; we’ll time a mid-December effective date for the anchor if you want to align to your Q1 budget.

Attachments: roi-modelmix-onepager.pdf (one-page numbers + model assumptions), anchor-stretch-proposal-draft.pdf (pricing mechanics). DocuSign link will be created post-call for the amendment draft: https://www.docusign.net/AMMPL-PL-2026-0043
